reasons.reader_question: The grip fails on 'they'll ca—' while she has the reins in hand. The reader leaves holding a concrete, dated question: three days, the Resin House, a cage.
reasons.change: Devan goes from guarded to poisoned on a clock. Raiu is dead. The informant has drained the lamps. Neela holds the plan, and Devan has lost the power to stop her.
reasons.romance_movement: The reason is new. He watches her choose to walk back into her own cage for him ('Nobody taught me this one... I'm choosing it'), and his reaching for her is useless. His side of the argument is thin: one loud 'No' and a single objection.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Each lead notices the other's body. She reads the colour of his lips and the grey in his face. He finds the split nails and touches one, and she lets him. Her name-saying over Raiu shows her habit becoming love. No narrated chemistry.
reasons.character_logic: Several choices are weak. Devan expects Vellan tonight and has found sabotaged lamps, yet he climbs the dark stair alone and sends his own door guard off alone for oil. The bear runs from one human woman with a knife and no reason is shown.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Her choice costs real things: the ache, a guild that knows she failed, trusting Muthu with his body, and three days on the clock. Raiu's death is paid for by Devan's own 'Hold the head' order, and Devan hears what it cost.
reasons.prose: Mostly concrete and quotable ('Its flame lay along the stone like a cut'). The opening logistics paragraph reads as a continuity patch, with an ambiguous 'Neela stood behind it'. 'Wet' appears four times in the fight. 'Flask corked' is repeated. Two consecutive paragraphs open with 'He'.
reasons.continuity: Conflicts with F245. There Neela reasons that only she and Muthu heard the order, but in this chapter she recites the order's terms to Devan in the stable.

fixes: Continuity (fails F245). In the stable, Neela says 'If I'm not back by first light on the second day, he's to bring you up the wood road'. That puts the order in Devan's hearing. Ch26 depends on only Neela and Muthu having heard it. Replace the specifics with 'I've told Muthu what to do if I'm late. Don't argue.' Keep the full terms offstage in her 'I need to talk to you outside' with Muthu, and record N2 as said there.

Irrational behaviour to extend plot. At 'The bear saw her. It dropped to all fours.', the retreat has no visible cause. A sloth bear that has just killed an armed guard would not run from one woman with a six-inch knife. Give Devan's POV a reason he can see. One option: she shouts 'Down! Both of you!' up the stair, and the stair-head pair come with spears and lamps, so Vellan faces three blades and light. Another: Devan sees her draw breath on a hard sound and stop, and the bear's eyes go to her mouth. That is a clue, but do not state that she is his witness.

Character logic and an exposition patch in the opening. In 'He could not spare the stair pair for an errand, so he had sent Raiu down', a smart warden who expects Vellan tonight strips his chamber door and climbs the sabotaged stair alone. Compress the paragraph to three lines and give a real reason. For example, the wall pairs are mid-change on the hour chain, and Raiu goes because the dark stair is the warden's own route to her door. Fix the ambiguous 'Neela stood behind it' so it reads as the barred chamber door. Cut the later repeat of 'with her flask corked'.
reader_question: Will Neela walk back into the Resin House to steal Devan's antidote, and can she come out uncaged before his three days run out?
new_facts_assessment: N1 (lamps drained, Raiu sent for oil) is useful because it sharpens the inside-informant thread. But it makes Devan look careless: he sends his only door guard off alone on a night he knows is the attack. N2 agrees with F244, but stating it in Devan's hearing breaks F245; the order should stay between Neela and Muthu. N3 is necessary to keep the Vellan-killed-Asha link closed until B2 ch16 per the secret map. The poison has to erase a thought instantly while killing slowly over three days, which edges toward contrived delay, so give the numbness one more sentence of physical onset before the thought goes. N4: 'four years dead' for Raiu's mother is unnecessary and echoes the retired F212 (Muthu's mother dead four years), which invites confusion in later passes. Cut the number. Devan at twenty-six at Asha's body is consistent with his age and F066. N5 is consistent with F160 and F231 and gives Devan a responsive-care detail. Accept it.
